record.paper_title: Some open problems in dynamical systems
record.original_question: For the complement G^∞_*(M) \ SE^∞_* of the stably-exponent class inside the space of smooth conservative or symplectic diffeomorphisms, which of the two Baire alternatives from §4.3 holds: generic zero exponent/entropy behavior, or the existence of a nonempty open set with entropy uniformly bounded below?

evidence.quote: c) On G∞ ∗ (M )−SE∞ ∗ , which of the two possibilities of 4.3 is true ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed smooth manifold equipped with either a smooth volume form or a smooth symplectic form, and let $G^\infty_*(M)$ denote, respectively, the space of $C^\infty$ volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$ or the space of $C^\infty$ symplectomorphisms of $M$, endowed with the $C^\infty$ topology. For $f\in G^\infty_*(M)$ and $x\in M$, let $\lambda_1(f,x)\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_{\dim M}(f,x)$ denote the Lyapunov exponents of $f$ at $x$ (defined almost everywhere with respect to the invariant volume). Say that $f$ has nonzero Lyapunov exponents stably if there is a $C^\infty$-neighborhood $\mathcal U$ of $f$ in $G^\infty_*(M)$ such that for every $g\in\mathcal U$ all Lyapunov exponents of $g$ are nonzero on a set of full volume (in the symplectic case, all $\dim M$ exponents are nonzero almost everywhere). Let $SE^\infty_*\subset G^\infty_*(M)$ be the set of such diffeomorphisms.

On the complement $G^\infty_*(M)\setminus SE^\infty_*$ (with its induced topology, which is a Baire space on any sufficiently regular open subset), decide which of the following two alternatives holds:

(A) There is a residual (dense $G_\delta$) subset $\mathcal R\subset G^\infty_*(M)\setminus SE^\infty_*$ such that every $f\in\mathcal R$ has vanishing Lyapunov exponents (and, in particular, vanishing metric entropy) almost everywhere; or

(B) There exists a nonempty open subset $\mathcal U\subset G^\infty_*(M)\setminus SE^\infty_*$ and a constant $c>0$ such that the metric entropy $h_{\mathrm{vol}}(g)\ge c$ for every $g\in\mathcal U$.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches for work by Bochi, Viana and others on generic Lyapunov-exponent dichotomies for conservative/symplectic diffeomorphisms in the $C^\infty$ topology turn up the known $C^1$ dichotomy (uniform hyperbolicity or zero exponents generically) and related results, but no resolution of the Baire dichotomy on the complement of the stably-nonzero-exponent class in the $C^\infty$ setting. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The Lyapunov exponents of generic volume-preserving and symplectic maps
status_evidence.snippet: Generic C^1 dichotomy: either dominated splitting or zero Lyapunov exponents almost everywhere.
status_evidence.claim: Bochi-Viana proved a C^1 dichotomy; the C^infty analogue and the dichotomy on the complement of SE remain open.

status_evidence.title: An isolated Lyapunov exponent (Bochi, 2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on Lyapunov exponents in conservative dynamics referencing open questions about exponents and entropy.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work indicates the smooth-topology Baire dichotomy questions of this type are still active and unresolved.
